page.text:
Induction and recursion represent the dual foundational aspects of the
successor structure on $\mathbb{N}$.
- *Mathematical induction* is the supreme method of proof: to verify that
  a proposition $P(n)$ holds for all natural numbers, it suffices to
  verify its truth at $0$ and show that truth is inherited from $n$ to
  $S(n)$.
- *Primitive recursion* is the supreme method of construction: to define
  a sequence or function on $\mathbb{N}$, it suffices to specify an
  initial value and a deterministic rule for stepping forward.

Both principles are logical manifestations of the same core fact:
$\mathbb{N}$ contains no spurious elements beyond those generated from
zero by repeated iteration of the successor function.
